```{r}
#| include: false
library(dplyr)
# Same source as the data catalogue: the weekly owdata harvest of the
# organisation (openwashdata/owdata#11). The strip counts published
# packages only, those whose CITATION.cff carries a Zenodo DOI (#174).
data <- readr::read_csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openwashdata/owdata/main/inst/extdata/owd_packages.csv",
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
published <- filter(data, as.logical(published) %in% TRUE)
n_pub <- nrow(published)
n_ds <- sum(published$n_datasets, na.rm = TRUE)
first_year <- min(as.integer(format(published$date, "%Y")), na.rm = TRUE)
n_years <- as.integer(format(Sys.Date(), "%Y")) - first_year + 1

# Teaching numbers from the graduate pages, one entry per capstone project.
graduate_files <- c(
  "pages/academy/graduates-2024/data/graduates.yml",
  "pages/academy/graduates-2026/data/graduates-2026.yml"
)
n_cohorts <- length(graduate_files)
n_projects <- sum(vapply(graduate_files, function(f) length(yaml::read_yaml(f)), integer(1)))

# Partner cards from the front matter of the partner pages.
partner_files <- sort(Sys.glob("pages/partners/*/index.qmd"))
partners <- lapply(partner_files, function(f) {
  fm <- rmarkdown::yaml_front_matter(f)
  list(
    title = fm$title,
    subtitle = if (is.null(fm$subtitle)) "" else fm$subtitle,
    href = sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", f)
  )
})
```

# Open data for water, sanitation and hygiene

<p class="owd-lead">openwashdata is an active global community that applies the FAIR principles to data from the water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) sector, and teaches the skills to do it.</p>

## Dataset of the month

::: {.owd-dotm}
::: {.owd-dotm-text}
**gwinfraassess** holds an assessment of 123 groundwater monitoring wells in Malawi by BASEflow Malawi in 2022 and 2023. Field teams recorded the condition of each well, its water level logger, the measuring equipment and what the well needs to keep working. Every well but one has an improvement plan, and the action named most often is a trained person to read the gauge (76 wells), ahead of a manual dipper (74 wells).

[Open gwinfraassess](https://openwashdata.github.io/gwinfraassess){.owd-more}
:::

::: {.owd-dotm-chart}

<p class="owd-chart-title">The most common fix is a person</p>
<p class="owd-chart-note">Share of the 122 wells with an improvement plan that need each action, coloured by kind of action. <span class="owd-chart-hint">Hover over a bar for the number of wells.</span></p>

```{r}
#| label: dataset-of-the-month-data
#| echo: false
# pak::pak("openwashdata/gwinfraassess")
library(gwinfraassess)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)

action_groups <- c(
  "Identify and training gauge reader" = "People",
  "Provide manual dipper" = "Equipment",
  "Replacement of the level logger" = "Equipment",
  "Installation of a new logger" = "Equipment",
  "Replace barologger" = "Equipment",
  "Rehabilitation of the civil works" = "Structure",
  "Replace end cap" = "Structure",
  "Replacement of the cover and hinges" = "Structure",
  "Welding on the existing hinges" = "Structure",
  "Replace and weld the hinges" = "Structure",
  "Redevelop the monitoring well" = "Structure",
  "Replace the well" = "Replace or retire",
  "Discard monitoring well" = "Replace or retire",
  "Discard as monitoring well and donate to the community" = "Replace or retire"
)

action_labels <- c(
  "Identify and training gauge reader" = "Find and train a gauge reader",
  "Provide manual dipper" = "Provide a manual dipper",
  "Replacement of the level logger" = "Replace the level logger",
  "Installation of a new logger" = "Install a new logger",
  "Replace barologger" = "Replace the barologger",
  "Rehabilitation of the civil works" = "Repair the civil works",
  "Replace end cap" = "Replace the end cap",
  "Replacement of the cover and hinges" = "Replace cover and hinges",
  "Welding on the existing hinges" = "Weld the existing hinges",
  "Replace and weld the hinges" = "Replace and weld the hinges",
  "Redevelop the monitoring well" = "Redevelop the well",
  "Replace the well" = "Replace the well",
  "Discard monitoring well" = "Discard the well",
  "Discard as monitoring well and donate to the community" = "Discard, give to community"
)

wells <- gwinfraassess |>
  mutate(well = row_number()) |>
  filter(!is.na(improvement_plan))

n_plans <- nrow(wells)

actions <- wells |>
  separate_longer_delim(improvement_plan, ",") |>
  mutate(action = gsub("\\s+", " ", trimws(improvement_plan))) |>
  filter(action %in% names(action_groups)) |>
  distinct(well, action) |>
  count(action, name = "n") |>
  mutate(
    group = unname(action_groups[action]),
    label = unname(action_labels[action]),
    share = round(100 * n / n_plans)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(n))

ojs_define(actions_data = actions, n_plans = n_plans)
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
actions = transpose(actions_data)

// width of the chart column, so the text keeps its size on every screen
chartWidth = Generators.observe((notify) => {
  const el = document.querySelector(".owd-dotm-chart");
  const report = () => notify(Math.max(280, el.clientWidth));
  const observer = new ResizeObserver(report);
  observer.observe(el);
  report();
  return () => observer.disconnect();
})

// chart-1, chart-3, chart-2 and a neutral grey from openwashdata/brand
palette = ["#8a3a8a", "#CF9E40", "#b04208", "#b9b9b9"]

Plot.plot({
  width: chartWidth,
  height: 400,
  marginLeft: chartWidth < 420 ? 170 : 200,
  marginRight: 36,
  marginTop: 4,
  marginBottom: 36,
  style: {fontFamily: "Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, sans-serif", fontSize: 13, background: "transparent"},
  ariaLabel: "Bar chart of improvement actions recommended for groundwater monitoring wells in Malawi",
  ariaDescription: "62 percent of wells need a trained gauge reader, 61 percent a manual dipper, 46 percent a replaced level logger and 42 percent repaired civil works.",
  x: {label: "% of wells", labelAnchor: "center", domain: [0, 70], grid: true, ticks: 4},
  y: {label: null, domain: actions.map((d) => d.label)},
  color: {
    domain: ["People", "Equipment", "Structure", "Replace or retire"],
    range: palette,
    legend: true
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(actions, {
      y: "label",
      x: "share",
      fill: "group",
      tip: true,
      title: (d) => `${d.label}\n${d.n} of ${n_plans} wells (${d.share}%)\n${d.group}`
    }),
    Plot.text(actions, {y: "label", x: "share", text: (d) => `${d.share}%`, textAnchor: "start", dx: 4, fill: "#1e1e1e"}),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

## Learn

<p class="owd-lead">We teach the skills to work with data in the open, free of charge, for people in the water, sanitation and hygiene sector.</p>

::: {.owd-learn}
::: {.owd-learn-card}
<span class="owd-card-kicker">Online course</span>
<strong>Data science for openwashdata</strong>
<p>Free and in R. Nine live sessions of 2.5 hours, exercises in between, and a capstone project on a dataset of your choice. Two cohorts have graduated since 2023. The course runs every second year, and the next one starts in September 2027.</p>

[About the course](pages/academy/index.qmd){.owd-more}
[Graduates 2026](pages/academy/graduates-2026/index.qmd){.owd-more}
:::

<strong>Workshops and a conference</strong>
<p>Next come in-person formats, week-long workshops and a conference. Subscribe to hear first.</p>

[Past events](pages/events/index.qmd){.owd-more}
[Subscribe](#subscribe){.owd-more}
:::
::: {.owd-learn-card}
<span class="owd-card-kicker">AI skills</span>
<strong>Working with AI on data</strong>
<p>The curriculum extends to AI skills, literacy and competency. We teach how to work with coding agents on data, with the same openness and review as everything else we publish.</p>

::: {.owd-why}
::: {.owd-why-intro}
## Why open data for WASH, and why now

<p class="owd-lead">Most WASH data is collected once, used for one report, and lost. The sector spends again to collect it again.</p>
:::
::: {.owd-why-points}
- **The data already exists.** Monitoring wells, waste surveys, sanitation inventories, refugee camp indicators. The datasets we publish were sitting in spreadsheets in organisations that wanted to share them and did not know how.
- **You own the result.** Your organisation stays the author and the copyright holder. The package lives in the open on GitHub, the deposit on Zenodo, and both can be moved anywhere.
- **The cost is your time.** Publishing is free. The tooling is open source, the review is done by the community, and the skills stay with you after the first package.
:::
:::

:::

::: {.owd-tint}
::: {.owd-section}

## How publishing works

<p class="owd-lead">Three steps, the same for every dataset, whether it has fifty rows or fifty thousand.</p>

::: {.owd-steps}
::: {.owd-step}
<span class="owd-step-number">1</span>
<strong>Prepare</strong>
<p>Our R package washr writes every file with a fixed shape. The raw data sits beside the processing script, a dictionary has one line per variable, and a README says what the data is and how it was collected. You write the prose.</p>
:::
::: {.owd-step}
<span class="owd-step-number">2</span>
<strong>Review</strong>
<p>A review against a versioned standard in four areas, metadata, data, documentation and tests. A script checks the mechanical items, a person checks the rest, and nothing is published before a check for personal data.</p>
:::
::: {.owd-step}
<span class="owd-step-number">3</span>
<strong>Publish</strong>
<p>A website for the package, a Zenodo DOI and a citation block. The licence is CC BY 4.0 by default, and you stay the author and the copyright holder.</p>
:::
:::

[Get started](pages/get-started/index.qmd){.owd-more}
[Donate data](https://github.com/openwashdata/data/issues){.owd-more}

:::

## Partners

<p class="owd-lead">Our partnerships are informal and based on a common interest in open data and code. They comprise contributors to the community and other open data initiatives in the WASH sector.</p>

```{r}
#| output: asis
# A raw HTML fence, so Pandoc does not wrap the cards in a paragraph.
cards <- vapply(partners, function(p) {
  sprintf(
    '<a class="owd-partner" href="%s"><strong>%s</strong>%s</a>',
    p$href,
    htmltools::htmlEscape(p$title),
    if (nzchar(p$subtitle)) sprintf("<span>%s</span>", htmltools::htmlEscape(p$subtitle)) else ""
  )
}, character(1))
cat("```{=html}\n<div class=\"owd-partners\">\n", paste(cards, collapse = "\n"), "\n</div>\n```\n", sep = "")
```
